children.text: The Volunteer Management System (VMS) will provide the City of Kamloops with a centralized online system for managing volunteers and connecting them with people and community groups that require assistance. The system is intended to improve the current manual volunteer management process, reduce assignment delays, improve planning, and encourage greater community participation.

children.text: After the COVID-19 pandemic, the City of Kamloops has lost contact with many of its volunteers. At the same time, the city has an increasing need for volunteers to support senior citizens, people with special needs, and students who require additional coaching and educational support. Currently, volunteer registration, verification, and assignment involve manual processes, which makes it difficult for the Mayor’s Office to maintain accurate information about volunteers and community needs. The proposed Volunteer Management System will provide a centralized platform where volunteers can register, be approved, have their activities recorded, and receive suitable assignments.

The city also does not have a centralized system that provides accurate information about the number of business risks. One major risk is insufficient volunteer participation. If there are not enough registered and approved volunteers, the system may not be able to support all reported cases. This risk can be reduced with the background-check system could delay volunteer approval and assignment. children.text:
The Volunteer Management System has the following measurable business objectives: 

  • Track at least 60% of senior cases requiring assistance in the city during the first year of operation. 

  •  Provide volunteer support to at least 85% of reported cases and reduce the volunteer assignment process so that people receive volunteer services within three days. 

  • Reduce unexpected volunteer shortages to fewer than two times per year by monitoring volunteer availability and providing daily forecasts of the expected cases for the following week.

attributesChanged.text: <Describe the important business objectives of the product in a way that is quantitative and measurable. Focus on the value provided to the business, including estimates of revenue or cost savings, return on investment analysis, or target release dates.>

children.text:
The success of the Volunteer Management System will be measured using the following metrics: 

  • The system should track at least 60% of senior cases in the city within the first year. 

  • At least 85% of reported cases should receive volunteer support, with assignments completed within three days. 

  • Unexpected volunteer shortages should occur fewer than two times per year. 

These metrics will help the Mayor’s Office determine whether the system is improving volunteer coordination, service delivery, and the city’s ability to plan for future community needs.

children.text:
The development and operation of the Volunteer Management System may involve several business risks. One major risk is insufficient volunteer participation. If there are not enough registered and approved volunteers, the system may not be able to support all reported cases. This risk can be reduced by providing incentives such as promotions and discounts from participating local businesses. 

Another risk is the dependency on the government’s automated police certificate system. Delays or technical problems with the background-check system could delay volunteer approval and assignment. The city should monitor this dependency and have appropriate procedures for handling verification delays. 

User adoption is also a potential risk. Volunteers and city staff may have difficulties adapting to the new system. Providing a simple interface, clear procedures, and appropriate training can help reduce this risk. 

Finally, inaccurate or outdated information about volunteer availability or community cases could result in unsuitable assignments. Regular updates and proper access controls can help maintain accurate information.

children.text:
The project is based on the following assumptions: 

  • The city will have enough volunteers willing to register and participate through the Volunteer Management System. 

  • The Mayor’s Office and authorized staff will maintain accurate information about volunteers and people requiring assistance. 

  • Local businesses will be willing to participate by providing promotions or discounts as incentives for volunteers. 

The system also has the following dependencies: 

  • The Volunteer Management System depends on the government’s automated police certificate system for volunteer background verification. The system is expected to process background checks within 48 hours. 

  • The system depends on participating local businesses to provide promotions and discounts that can encourage volunteer participation. 

  • The system depends on reliable internet access and suitable technical infrastructure so that volunteers and authorized city staff can access the online system.

children.text: The Volunteer Management System (VMS) will be designed to organize and improve the way volunteers are managed and assigned to people who require assistance. The system will primarily support senior citizens by providing services such as regular check-in calls and wellness education. It will also assist students who require extra coaching or academic support. The VMS will store and manage important volunteer information, including qualifications, availability, background-check status, assigned cases, and current volunteer demand. One of the main objectives is to shorten the volunteer assignment process from approximately two weeks to three days and help prevent unexpected shortages of volunteers.

children.text:
The main features of the VMS will include:

1 - Volunteer Registration: allow administrators to add and manage volunteer information.

2 - Availability Tracking: record when volunteers are available to provide services.

3 - Qualification Tracking: keep track of volunteer skills, qualifications, and areas of expertise.

4 - Background-Check Tracking: monitor whether a volunteer's required background check has been completed or is still pending.

5 - Case Management: record and organize information about individuals who require support.

6 - Volunteer Matching: match qualified volunteers with senior citizens or students based on their needs, qualifications, and availability.

7 - Assignment Management: allow administrators to assign volunteers to specific cases.

8 - Demand Forecasting: estimate future volunteer requirements based on current and expected demand.

 9 - Notifications: send daily alerts and updates to administrators about volunteer needs, assignments, and possible shortages.

The first version of the VMS will include the essential features needed to address the city's current problems such as:

- Volunteer management.

- Case management.

- Background-check status tracking.

- Volunteer matching.

- Volunteer assignment.

- Volunteer demand forecasting.

- Notifications and alerts.

- Ability to track 60% of senior cases

- Ability to provide support for 85% of reported cases

- Reduce volunteer assignment time to three days

Future versions of the system may include:

- Advanced reports and data analysis.

- More accurate demand forecasting.

- Support for additional community services.

- Improved volunteer reward and recognition programs.

- Integration with other city or government systems.

- Additional features based on feedback from administrators and volunteers.

attributesChanged.text: <If a staged evolution of the product is envisioned over time, indicate which major features will be deferred to later releases.>

children.text:
The following items will be outside the scope of the initial system:

  • The VMS will not conduct police background checks itself. Instead, it will rely on the government's external background-check system.

  • The system will not provide medical services.

  • The system will not provide emergency services.

  • The system will not replace teachers.

  • The system will not replace existing online education platforms.

  • The system cannot guarantee that every case will receive a volunteer because volunteer availability may be limited.

  • Volunteer services outside the main focus of senior support and student coaching will not be included in the initial release.

  • Additional types of volunteer services may be considered for future releases.

children.text: Some issues and concerns with the project are the current system is a long process and is not always accurate with the data, the education administrator is concerned about younger kids needing more support or have special cases, and lastly concerns of having a volunteer shortage. The new system will be much faster and accurate, and within the first year should track 60% of senior cases and provide support to 85% of those cases. By having online services and volunteers with the proper knowledge and skills to help with the special cases for the younger kids. Having a notification system for the upcoming weeks and prioritizing the seniors within 3 days will help with the volunteer shortage. The major customers are the seniors, younger kids, and businesses. The seniors need all the support they can get because they are the most at risk, the younger kids need support and help especially with special cases, and the businesses need more customers and to promote volunteering while reducing crime rate. The management priorities are making sure the city has volunteers and having a system that is easy and efficient, while prioritizing the support and help for seniors, younger kids, and businesses.
